skill.name: insforge
skill.description: Guides app development with InsForge SDK across database, authentication, storage, functions, realtime, email, OpenRouter AI, payments, and S3-compatible tooling.
skill.summary: Build InsForge application features with secure SDK and service integration patterns.
skill.author: insforge

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are scanner noise from Markdown, placeholders, environment configuration, relative links, and documented provider endpoints. Confirmed risks include dynamic URL fetching and outbound email capability. Semantic review found unsafe RAG trust placement, consentless feedback, browser email abuse, unpinned package execution, and payment fulfillment flaws.

remediation.issue: Retrieved documents are inserted into a system-role message.
remediation.suggestion: Keep application instructions separate, label retrieved text as untrusted data, add prompt-injection defenses, and restrict model tools and data access.

remediation.issue: The feedback workflow can send project details without explicit consent.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before submission and show the exact redacted payload, destination, and command to the user.

remediation.issue: Signed-in browser users can call the custom email API directly.
remediation.suggestion: Route email through server code that enforces roles, approved templates, recipient rules, quotas, and audit logging.

remediation.issue: A server example fetches an externally supplied image URL.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist HTTPS hosts, reject private and link-local addresses, limit redirects and response size, and stream downloads with timeouts.

remediation.issue: Setup commands execute unpinned packages with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed SDK and CLI versions, avoid automatic npx confirmation, and require approval before installing or running downloaded packages.

remediation.issue: One-time payment fulfillment does not validate the purchased value.
remediation.suggestion: Create checkout terms from server-owned order data and compare provider, environment, product, amount, currency, and payment status before marking an order paid.

remediation.issue: Subscription fulfillment grants a fixed plan without checking the purchased product.
remediation.suggestion: Map verified provider price or plan identifiers to entitlements server-side and reject unknown, mismatched, test, refunded, or incomplete purchases.

content.value_statement: Building InsForge features requires correct SDK, authentication, storage, AI, and payment patterns. This skill provides focused implementation guidance and production-oriented examples.
actual_capabilities: Creates InsForge SDK clients for browser, server, and SSR applications.
Guides database CRUD, filters, pagination, RPC calls, and row-level security.
Implements authentication, sessions, OAuth callbacks, password reset, and profile flows.
Covers storage uploads, downloads, deletion, S3-compatible tools, and storage policies.
Integrates OpenRouter chat, images, video, audio, embeddings, and RAG.
Builds realtime, transactional email, Stripe, Razorpay, and edge function workflows.
limitations: Infrastructure changes, deployments, migrations, and provider setup require the separate InsForge CLI workflow.
Examples require adaptation to the application schema, authorization model, and framework.
OpenRouter and payment features require configured external accounts, keys, and supported plans.
The skill provides guidance and examples but does not verify production configuration automatically.

use_cases.title: Launch a SaaS Application
use_cases.description: Build authentication, database records, uploads, subscriptions, and transactional emails with InsForge services.

use_cases.title: Add AI Product Features
use_cases.description: Connect OpenRouter models to InsForge storage, vector search, job tracking, and protected application data.

use_cases.title: Modernize Existing Integrations
use_cases.description: Move existing S3, Stripe, Razorpay, and realtime workflows onto documented InsForge SDK patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an InsForge client for my [framework] application. Use the correct environment variables and explain where each value belongs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new application

prompt_templates.title: Build Authenticated CRUD
prompt_templates.prompt: Add sign-in and CRUD for [resource]. Derive ownership from the session, handle errors, and describe the required row-level security.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Paid File Workflows
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [Stripe or Razorpay] checkout flow with protected file access. Include webhook fulfillment, storage keys, and user-visible states.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production RAG System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an InsForge RAG pipeline for [content]. Include schema, embeddings, tenant isolation, prompt-injection controls, evaluation, and bounded server processing.

output_examples.input: Add email and password authentication to a Next.js application.
output: A server and browser client structure using InsForge SSR helpers.
Sign-up, sign-in, callback, refresh, and sign-out flow guidance.
Cookie, redirect, error handling, and session security notes.

output_examples.input: Create a user-owned image upload feature.
output: An upload workflow that stores both the public URL and object key.
Authentication and storage policy requirements for user ownership.
Download, replacement, and deletion behavior with error states.
Checkout and customer portal flow guidance.
Required payment table policies and subject ownership rules.

best_practices: Keep admin and OpenRouter keys in server-only environment variables.
Derive ownership from authenticated sessions and enforce row-level security for every protected table.
Pin dependencies, validate external URLs, and require confirmation before networked administrative actions.
anti_patterns: Do not place admin, payment, S3, or OpenRouter secrets in browser bundles.
Do not trust browser-supplied ownership, prices, plan identifiers, or payment status.
Do not fulfill payments from success pages or store temporary media URLs as durable assets.

faq.question: Which InsForge features does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers SDK integration for data, auth, storage, functions, AI, realtime, email, Stripe, Razorpay, and S3-compatible tools.

faq.question: Does this skill manage infrastructure?
faq.answer: No. Use the InsForge CLI workflow for migrations, deployments, secrets, provider configuration, buckets, functions, and schedules.

faq.question: Can I use it with Next.js SSR?
faq.answer: Yes. The guides cover browser clients, server clients, auth actions, middleware refresh, callbacks, and secure cookie handling.

faq.question: Can browser code use an InsForge anon key?
faq.answer: Yes. Anon keys support user-scoped clients, but row-level security and authenticated sessions must protect application data.

faq.question: Does it support AI features?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers OpenRouter chat, images, video, audio, embeddings, model discovery, and RAG with InsForge storage and data.

faq.question: What must I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review authorization, row-level security, secret placement, package versions, external URL validation, email permissions, payment webhooks, and plan limits.
